alerts.name: Cross-Domain Misconfiguration
alerts.description: Web browser data loading may be possible, due to a Cross Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) misconfiguration on the web server.
alerts.solution: Ensure that sensitive data is not available in an unauthenticated manner (using IP address white-listing, for instance). Configure the "Access-Control-Allow-Origin" HTTP header to a more restrictive set of domains, or remove all CORS headers entirely, to allow the web browser to enforce the Same Origin Policy (SOP) in a more restrictive manner.
alerts.review: Se conserva la clasificación automática. Contrastar CORS de recursos públicos con el rechazo de orígenes ajenos en API autenticada; no equivale por sí solo a una fuga de datos privados.

alerts.name: Re-examine Cache-control Directives
alerts.description: The cache-control header has not been set properly or is missing, allowing the browser and proxies to cache content. For static assets like css, js, or image files this might be intended, however, the resources should be reviewed to ensure that no sensitive content will be cached.
alerts.solution: For secure content, ensure the cache-control HTTP header is set with "no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate". If an asset should be cached consider setting the directives "public, max-age, immutable".
alerts.review: Interpretar junto con las cabeceras no-store, el contraste de dos cuentas y el rechazo del acceso anónimo. Una cabecera de caché por sí sola no demuestra mezcla de datos.

alerts.name: Information Disclosure - Suspicious Comments
alerts.description: The response appears to contain suspicious comments which may help an attacker.
alerts.solution: Remove all comments that return information that may help an attacker and fix any underlying problems they refer to.
alerts.review: La detección de comentarios es informativa y no demuestra por sí sola una contraseña o dato privado expuesto. No se publica la evidencia cruda.

alerts.name: Retrieved from Cache
alerts.description: The content was retrieved from a shared cache. If the response data is sensitive, personal or user-specific, this may result in sensitive information being leaked. In some cases, this may even result in a user gaining complete control of the session of another user, depending on the configuration of the caching components in use in their environment. This is primarily an issue where caching servers such as "proxy" caches are configured on the local network. This configuration is typically found in corporate or educational environments, for instance.
alerts.solution: Validate that the response does not contain sensitive, personal or user-specific information. If it does, consider the use of the following HTTP response headers, to limit, or prevent the content being stored and retrieved from the cache by another user: Cache-Control: no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate, private Pragma: no-cache Expires: 0 This configuration directs both HTTP 1.0 and HTTP 1.1 compliant caching servers to not store the response, and to not retrieve the response (without validation) from the cache, in response to a similar request.
alerts.review: Interpretar junto con las cabeceras no-store, el contraste de dos cuentas y el rechazo del acceso anónimo. Una cabecera de caché por sí sola no demuestra mezcla de datos.

alerts.solution: This is an informational alert and so no changes are required.
alerts.review: Observación informativa; no demuestra una vulnerabilidad explotable.
